components.text: Explain why fine-tuning and mathematical intelligibility favor purposive mind over unguided alternatives.
Whether fine-tuning and mathematical intelligibility are comparatively better explained by purposive mind.
Show why undefeated personal experience can justify Christianity rather than incompatible religious conclusions under the same standard.
Distinguish rational disagreement from standards permissive enough to validate mutually inconsistent religious claims.
Whether undefeated personal experience or objective investigation can rationally support Christianity specifically.
Whether differing personally valid reasons suffice while all parties still owe good reasons for belief.
Explain why uneven personal experience and indirect transmission remain expected if an omnipotent loving God wants Christian belief.
Explain why widespread disagreement is merely rational diversity rather than evidence against clear divine communication.
Whether personal experience and intellectual investigation supply adequate and reasonably accessible Christian warrant.
Whether reasonable disagreement can persist without counting against the rationality of Christianity.
Show that causally determined belief cannot count as rational unless a person freely chooses that belief.
Whether rational belief requires libertarian freedom from wholly material causal determination.
Provide a non-theistic account of moral reasons, social rules, and human interests sufficient to resist unique Christian grounding.
Whether non-theistic resources can account for moral reasons, cooperation, and human value without divine grounding.
Explain how the child's punitive death can be reconciled with the goodness of an omnipotent and omnibenevolent God.
Whether the narrative's punishment of David through his innocent child's death defeats Christianity's claim about a good God.
Supply evidence proportionate to resurrection and defend transmitted testimony as reliable enough for the extraordinary conclusion.
Show why subjective experience can carry adequate weight for specifically supernatural Christian claims.
Whether transmitted historical claims provide evidence strong enough to make resurrection the best explanation of the asserted facts.
Whether scriptural transmission and interpretation reliably support specifically Christian conclusions.
Show that establishing resurrection would warrant the further specifically Christian conclusion about Jesus's divine identity.
Whether resurrection, even if established, supports the specifically Christian conclusion about Jesus's divine identity and authority.
Show that Christian testimony is textually recoverable, early, and connected to eyewitness or preserved early tradition.
Whether textual transmission and historical testimony are reliable and proximate enough to contribute proportionate evidence for Christian claims.
Whether the available sources preserve contextual material capable of supporting a Christian-specific identity inference.
Answer the claim that Christian interpretation of nature followed external scientific correction rather than clear revelation.
Whether scientific scrutiny undermines the legitimacy of Christianity's present explanatory appeal to fine-tuning.
Explain why reasons-responsive rationality remains trustworthy if evolved cognition is selected primarily for survival rather than truth.
Whether evidence-responsive rationality remains trustworthy when cognition is wholly produced by evolution and natural causes.
Explain how fallible evolved cognition can earn rational trust through verification despite lacking certainty.
Show why epistemic discomfort or uncertainty does not warrant inferring a divine guarantor of reason.
Whether evolved, fallible cognition can remain rationally usable and trustworthy under naturalism.
Whether uncertainty and causal limitation require adopting God as a guarantor of rational belief.
